- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots and forecasts too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is near 70–71, model frequently overestimates upward momentum; cap forecast at +1.5% above current price unless strong bullish sentiment persists.  
- Model underestimates true price drops when sentiment is negative and recent price is above 70; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast to avoid under-shock.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underpredicts upward moves after negative sentiment; add 0.3–0.7% upward bias if sentiment is negative and price is below 68.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; increase forecast variance by 0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
